metadata.unit_slo: Review the key concepts of 1. Introduction to AI concepts.

evaluation_context.goal: Produce an excellent, source-faithful learner session while preserving all deterministic correctness, identity, and sequence constraints.
evaluation_context.source_fidelity_goal: Independently verify the hard-gated edited challenger against the supplied source material. Reject unsupported facts, answers, explanations, feedback, or terminology changes; do not edit the artifact.

criteria.factual_fidelity: Every claim and answer is faithful to the supplied source.
criteria.answer_unambiguity: Each item has one defensible answer under its instructions.
criteria.distractor_plausibility: Distractors are credible without becoming defensible answers.
criteria.misconception_quality: Wrong choices diagnose realistic learner misconceptions.
criteria.cognitive_progression: The ordered session builds understanding at a coherent pace.
criteria.mechanic_rhythm_variation: Mechanics vary naturally without disruptive repetition.
criteria.scenario_authenticity: Scenarios resemble credible decisions or tasks.
criteria.feedback_usefulness: Feedback explains the governing concept and next step.
criteria.difficulty_appropriateness: Difficulty matches the stated audience and session position.
criteria.terminology_consistency: Terms are used consistently with the source and across items.
criteria.overall_learner_experience: The exact final sequence is coherent, varied, and instructive.

evidence.statement: The item claims and keyed answers consistently match the authoritative source, including generative AI, speech, NLP, information extraction, agents, and responsible handling of PII.
Items generally provide one defensible answer or an explicit set of correct selections; the speech-recognition item has misleading incorrect-answer feedback, but its keyed answer remains unambiguous.
Distractors are mostly credible category confusions, such as language detection versus sentiment analysis and OCR versus speech-to-text.
Wrong-choice rationales diagnose realistic confusions between generation, classification, summarization, entity extraction, speech processing, and agent components.
The sequence covers many concepts but alternates topics irregularly and places basic remembering items after higher-rung application and evaluation items, weakening a coherent instructional build.
The 24-item session uses multiple-choice, true/false, fill-blank, and arrange-sentence mechanics with no disruptive long run of one mechanic.
Prompt stems vary across definitions, scenarios, selections, reconstruction, and direct questions, though several arrange-sentence prompts use similar wording.
Applied scenarios are credible and source-aligned, including receipt processing, museum assistance, multilingual support, customer-feedback privacy, and component serial-number extraction.

Most incorrect-option feedback explains the misconception and gives a better-fit concept, but one feedback statement incorrectly says a recorded conversation would not be a transcription task, despite the source listing call and meeting transcription as speech uses.
The checkpoint appropriately mixes foundational recall with applied scenarios and higher-rung distinctions, although the ordering sometimes places recall after more advanced applications.
Core terms are used consistently with the source, including language model, AI agent, action tool, speech recognition, speech synthesis, OCR, summarization, and PII redaction.
The session is broad, accurate, varied, and generally instructive, but its topic sequencing is less coherent than ideal and one feedback statement is misleading.

largest_gap.summary: The incorrect-answer intrinsic feedback for the speech-recognition item contradicts the source's transcription examples.

evidence.statement: The feedback says a recorded conversation would not be correctly described as a transcription task, while the authoritative source explicitly lists automated transcription of calls or meetings as a common AI speech use.

largest_gap.repair_instruction: Within the existing item, replace only the incorrect-answer intrinsic feedback with a source-faithful explanation such as: "Speech recognition commonly transcribes spoken audio into text, so a recorded conversation can be a transcription task." Preserve question_type and all correctness data.

result.concise_summary: The artifact is highly source-faithful and mechanically varied, with strong distractors and realistic scenarios. The largest repairable gap is one misleading speech-recognition feedback statement; sequence coherence is also somewhat weaker but does not require human review.
